idiom_name: node types with named child fields + per-node traversal
implementation_notes: Give each grammar-production alternative its own node type and replace the positional children collection with a named, typed field per child role (left, right, condition, body). Keep the few cross-cutting payloads - source token or span, computed type - in a common base type so nodes still share them, and implement printing, evaluation and rewriting as node-specific operations that read the named fields directly. Accept that every generic walk must be written per node type, and expect the duplication to grow with the number of passes. Choose this form when readability and node-local invariants dominate; switch to a uniform child list (or an algebraic data type with exhaustive matching) when many generic passes must traverse arbitrary subtrees.
pitfalls: Letting node-specific operations absorb traversal: once generic walking over named fields is attempted, per-node knowledge leaks into every analysis and the duplication is invisible until an analysis is added.
Exposing mutable child fields publicly, so the arity and type invariants the field names promise can be broken after construction.
Forgetting the common base for cross-cutting data (spans, types), which forces every node to re-implement it or every pass to special-case nodes.
Using mutable public fields instead of constructor-validated immutable references, so client code can silently break arity invariants after construction.
Creating a deep inheritance hierarchy for node types instead of a flat type-per-alternative structure, which forces every operation to walk the hierarchy and complicates adding new node types.
Naming fields inconsistently across node types (e.g., 'condition' in If but 'test' in While) without a documented convention, forcing consumers to memorise per-type mappings.

Wrong move: assume one generalizing visitor chain covers every overlapping AST capability -> clients silently miss nodes on the hierarchy axis the chain did not choose -> instead use explicit pattern checks or a unifying traversal when capabilities overlap.

Wrong move: enumerate named fields manually in every generic pass -> optional and repeated children are easy to omit and traversal logic drifts -> instead centralize or generate field-aware traversal before adding more node-specific passes.

Wrong move: choose named fields for a cache-oriented batch pipeline -> heterogeneous layouts defeat uniform storage and bulk passes pay repeated dispatch costs -> instead expose a normalized secondary view while retaining named fields for node-local semantics.
